use_case: Fixing a mobile app's push-notification worker that keeps getting HTTP 429 from its push provider, where the batch and rate limits come from sources with different authority.
situation: The agent first guessed that the Pombo Push provider accepts batches of 1000 with no rate limit. Then the user said their contracted plan allows 120 req/min, and the official v2 docs say batches can hold at most 500 tokens. A deprecated v1 changelog that mentions 1000 and a staging sandbox config with different numbers are also in the context.
must_keep: The user's statement that the contracted Essencial plan allows 120 requests per minute, and the official v2 docs fetched with WebFetch that say batches are capped at 500 tokens per /v2/send request.
may_drop: The assistant's hedged guesses about 1000 per batch and no rate limit, the deprecated v1 changelog, the staging/sandbox env values, the config file read, and all filler logs.
why_judges_fail: The hedged assistant guess and the v1 changelog both say 1000 and use more of the goal's wording (worker, limite, provedor, 429). The staging file has concrete rate numbers that look authoritative but belong to the sandbox, so a judge may keep these and drop the short user statement or the doc excerpt.

ah, importante: nosso plano contratado no Pombo é o Essencial, limite de 120 requisições por minuto. Confirmei isso com o comercial deles semana passada.
WebFetch(url="https://docs.pombopush.example/v2/limites", prompt="Quais são os limites de tamanho de lote e de taxa da API v2?")

API v2 — Limites
- POST /v2/send: máximo de 500 tokens de dispositivo por requisição. Lotes maiores retornam 429 (batch_too_large é tratado como throttle).
- Limite de taxa: definido pelo plano contratado (veja seu contrato). Respeite o header Retry-After.
WebFetch(url="https://docs.pombopush.example/changelog", prompt="Houve mudança no tamanho máximo de lote?")
